::: {.key-question}
What chronic health conditions are experienced by Aboriginal and/or Torres Strait Islander peoples in the NEPHU catchment?
:::

## Asthma

### Self-Reported Asthma

```{r}
# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Asthma, by LGA
# Data from ABS Census using TableBuilderPro
# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Read in Census data
asthma_lga <- f_read_census_lga("Aboriginal_Health_Asthma_LGA.csv",
                                variable = "asthma") %>% 
  #
  dplyr::filter(asthma != "Not stated")

# Data wrangling
asthma_lga <- asthma_lga %>%
  #
  dplyr::mutate(asthma = dplyr::case_when(
    asthma == "Has asthma" ~ "yes",
    TRUE ~ "no")) %>% 
  #
  f_wrangle_census_lga(variable = asthma,
                       level    = "person",
                       dichot   = "yes")

# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Asthma, by age and sex
# Data from ABS Census using TableBuilderPro
# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Read in Census data
asthma_agesex <- f_read_census_agesex("Aboriginal_Health_Asthma_AgeSex.csv",
                                      variable = "asthma") %>% 
  #
  dplyr::filter(asthma != "Not stated")

# Data wrangling
asthma_agesex <- asthma_agesex %>% 
  #
  dplyr::mutate(asthma = dplyr::case_when(
    asthma == "Has asthma" ~ "yes",
    TRUE ~ "no")) %>%  
  #
  f_wrangle_census_agesex(variable = asthma,
                          dichot   = "yes")
```

- Data for this topic were obtained from the [ABS Census 2021](https://www.abs.gov.au/census).

- Overall, 17% (n = 1,902) of people living in the NEPHU catchment who identified as Aboriginal and/or Torres Strait Islander in the Census have been told by a doctor or nurse that they have asthma. This was higher than for non-Indigenous people living in the NEPHU catchment (8.5%).

- The number of people living in different LGAs within the NEPHU catchment who identified as Aboriginal and/or Torres Strait Islander in the Census who have been told by a doctor or nurse that they have asthma ranged from 388 (Whittlesea LGA) to 25 (Manningham LGA).

- The gap between the observed number of Aboriginal and/or Torres Strait Islander people who have been told by a doctor or nurse that they have asthma and the number expected if the rate was the same as for non-Indigenous people was biggest for Whittlesea and Hume LGAs.

- The percentage of people living in different LGAs within the NEPHU catchment who identified as Aboriginal and/or Torres Strait Islander in the Census who have been told by a doctor or nurse that they have asthma ranged from 18% (Maroondah, Whittlesea, and Hume LGAs) to 8.8% (Manningham LGA).

- The number of people who have been told by a doctor or nurse that they have asthma was highest for people aged 20-29 years for both males and females.

::: {.callout-tip title="Question/s asked for this topic" icon=false collapse=false}
The following question was asked of all people completing the ABS Census 2021.

- Has the person been told by a doctor or nurse that they have any of these long-term health conditions? (Select all that apply)
  - Arthritis
  - Asthma
  - Cancer (including remission)
  - Dementia (including Alzheimer's)
  - Diabetes (excluding gestational diabetes)
  - Heart disease (including heart attack or angina)
  - Kidney disease
  - Lung condition (including COPD or emphysema)
  - Mental health condition (including depression or anxiety)
  - Stroke
  - Any other long-term health condition(s)
  - No long-term health condition

<div style="height: 2em;"></div>
:::

### Hospital Admissions

```{r}
# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Hospitalisations - asthma
# Data from PHIDU Social Health Atlas
# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Read in PHIDU data
hospital_asthma <- f_read_phidu_iare_hospital(data_sheet    = "Admissions_principal_diag",
                                              column_select = "admissions_for_asthma_aboriginal_people")

# Data wrangling
hospital_asthma <- hospital_asthma %>% 
  dplyr::mutate(iare_name = factor(iare_name, levels = iare_inc_vic_lvl)) %>% 
  #
  dplyr::arrange(iare_name)
```

- Data for this topic were obtained from the [PHIDU Social Health Atlas](https://phidu.torrens.edu.au/social-health-atlases).

- During the four-year period 01 July 2017 to 30 June 2021 there were 292 hospital admissions for asthma for Aboriginal and/or Torres Strait Islander people living in Greater Melbourne.

- The number of admissions for asthma for Aboriginal and/or Torres Strait Islander people living in different IAREs within the NEPHU catchment ranged from 51 (Northcote/Preston/Whittlesea IARE) to 6 (Melbourne East IARE).

- The age-standardised rate of admissions for asthma for Aboriginal and/or Torres Strait Islander people living in different IAREs within the NEPHU catchment ranged from 287 per 100,000 population (Northcote/Preston/Whittlesea IARE) to 93 per 100,000 population (Melbourne East IARE).

- 3 of the 8 IAREs in the NEPHU catchment area with data available for reporting had an age-standardised admission rate for asthma above the average rate for all Aboriginal and/or Torres Strait Islander people living in Greater Melbourne (Northcote/Preston/Whittlesea, Yarra Ranges, and Moreland/Broadmeadows IAREs).

::: {.callout-tip title="ICD-10-AM codes and definitions for this topic" icon=false collapse=false}
Admissions for asthma are defined as those with a principal diagnosis code in the following list, coded using the [International Statistical Classification of Diseases and Related Health Problems 10th Revision Australian Modification (ICD-10-AM)](https://www.ihacpa.gov.au/health-care/classification/icd-10-amachiacs):

  - J45.0: Predominantly allergic asthma
  - J45.1: Non-allergic asthma
  - J45.8: Mixed asthma
  - J45.9: Asthma (unspecified)
  - J46: Status asthmaticus

<div style="height: 2em;"></div>
:::

## Self-Reported Allergic Rhinitis

```{r}
# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Allergic rhinitis (hay fever)
# Data from ABS National Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Health Survey
# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Read in NATSIHS data
allergy <- f_read_natsihs_sex("Indicator_Vic_Sex_Chronic_Conditions.csv")

# Data wrangling
allergy <- allergy %>% 
  dplyr::rowwise() %>% 
  dplyr::mutate(noallergy_n = total_n - hay_fever_and_allergic_rhinitis_n) %>% 
  dplyr::ungroup() %>% 
  #
  janitor::adorn_totals(fill = "Total") %>%
  #
  dplyr::rename(yesallergy_n = hay_fever_and_allergic_rhinitis_n,
                answered_n   = total_n) %>% 
  #
  dplyr::mutate(yesallergy_prop = yesallergy_n / answered_n * 100,
                noallergy_prop  = noallergy_n / answered_n * 100,
                answered_prop   = answered_n / answered_n * 100) %>% 
  #
  dplyr::select(sex,
                starts_with("yesallergy"),
                starts_with("noallergy"),
                starts_with("answered")) %>% 
  #
  tidyr::pivot_longer(!sex,
                      names_to = c("answer", ".value"),
                      names_pattern = "(.+)_(.+)") %>% 
  #
  dplyr::mutate(answer = factor(dplyr::recode(answer,
                                              "yesallergy" = "Yes",
                                              "noallergy"  = "No",
                                              "answered"   = "Total"),
                                levels = c("Yes",
                                           "No",
                                           "Total")))
```

- Data for this topic were obtained from the [2022-23 ABS National Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Health Survey](https://www.abs.gov.au/statistics/people/aboriginal-and-torres-strait-islander-peoples/national-aboriginal-and-torres-strait-islander-health-survey/latest-release).

- Overall, 37% of Aboriginal and/or Torres Strait Islander survey respondents living in Greater Melbourne reported that they were living with allergic rhinitis (hay fever). This equates to approximately 14,200 Aboriginal and/or Torres Strait Islander people.

- The percentage of people living with allergic rhinitis (hay fever) was similar for males and females (36% vs. 37%).

::: {.callout-tip title="Question/s asked for this topic" icon=false collapse=false}
The following questions were asked of all people completing the 2022-23 ABS National Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Health Survey.

- Do you have any of the following conditions that have lasted, or are expected to last, for six months or longer? (Select all that apply)
  - Hay fever
  - Sinusitis or sinus allergy
  - Food allergy
  - Drug allergy
  - Anaemia
  - Bronchitis
  - Endometriosis
  - Polycystic ovary syndrome (PCOS)
  - Fluid problems, fluid retention, or oedema (excluding those due to a heart or circulatory condition)
  - Hernias
  - Kidney stones
  - Migraine
  - Psoriasis
  - Stomach ulcers or other gastrointestinal ulcers
  - Thyroid trouble or goitre
  - Slipped disc or other disc problems
  - Back pain or other back problems
  - None of the above
  
<div style="height: 1em;"></div>

- If yes, were you told that you have this condition by a doctor or nurse?
  - Yes
  - No

<div style="height: 2em;"></div>
:::

#### Table 10D-4

::: {#tab_10D_4 .fig-tab-title}
**Table 10D-4:** Self-reported allergic rhinitis (hay fever) for people who identified as Aboriginal and/or Torres Strait Islander, Victoria, by sex, 2022-2023
:::

```{r}
#
table_count  <- table_count + 1
table_number <- paste0("Table_", table_section, "_", sprintf("%.02d", table_count))

table <- allergy %>% 
  tidyr::pivot_wider(names_from  = "sex",
                     values_from = c("n", "prop"),
                     names_vary  = "slowest") %>% 
  #
  janitor::clean_names() %>% 
  #
  dplyr::rename(allergic_rhinitis = answer)

if (!file.exists(paste0(here::here(), "/data/", table_number, ".csv"))) {
  
  write.csv(table, paste0(here::here(), "/data/", table_number, ".csv"), row.names = FALSE)
  
}

table %>% 
  dplyr::mutate(prop_male   = sprintf("%.1f", prop_male),
                prop_female = sprintf("%.1f", prop_female),
                prop_total  = sprintf("%.1f", prop_total)) %>%
  #
  f_table_grouped_sex(n_variable  = "estimate",
                      column_name = "Allergic rhinitis<br>(hay fever)")
```
